Mitākṣarā
(‘[a work with] limited number of letters,’ ‘a small work’)
------------------------------------------
A Hindu’s life, at the personal as well as the social level, has been regulated by the धर्मशास्त्रस् for over two millennia. The Yājñavalkyasmṛti, a metrical work in about a thousand verses, is one of the earliest and most authoritative works. It has several commentaries out of which the Mitākṣarā of विज्ञानेश्वर (circa A.

) has been considered outstanding.
Vijñāneśvara was an expert in Pūrva-Mīmāṁsā Darśana and applies its rules for determining the purpose of the Smṛti of याज्ञवल्क्य wherever there is doubt.
Though the Mitākṣarā—also termed Ṛjumitākṣarā and Pramitākṣarā—is generally brief and clear, as the very name indicates, it also goes into great details when needed.
The work quotes about 80 smṛtis and writers of धर्मशास्त्रस्. An interesting factor noticed is that it almost ignores the पुराणस्. Only five पुराणस् have been quoted. Other, earlier, authors quoted by it are विश्वरूप (circa A.

).
The Mitākṣarā has several commentaries out of which the following are more noteworthy: Subodhinī of Viśveśvara-भट्ट (14th century A. D.); Pramitākṣarā of नन्दपण्डित (A.

-1820).
There is also another Mitākṣarā which is a commentary on the Gautama-dharmasūtras by हरदत्त (circa A.

Mitra
(‘the friend’)
------------------------------------------
Mitra is one of the important deities praised in the Ṛgveda. More often, he is praised along with वरुण, another Vedic god. He is one of the twelve Ādityas (aspects of the Sungod, सूर्य). He resides in the अन्तरिक्ष or sky and gives us rain. He impels the people of the world towards constructive activity. He unites people with mutual love and friendship. He sustains the world, protects it and is capable of bestowing boons (vide Ṛgveda 3.59.1, 2 and 7).
The word ‘mitra’ has been used in a technical sense in political science, to indicate an ally of a king. A मित्र had to be courted either by sāma (spirit of reconciliation) or by दान (the spirit of give and take).
While मैत्री or an attitude of friendship has been recommended by the Yoga-sūtras (1.33) as an aid to concentration of मिन्द्, the characteristics of a true friend (mitra) are described as follows: He will prevent you from committing sins. On the other hand he will encourage you to do good deeds. He will keep your secrets. He will praise your good qualities openly. He will not desert you in your periods of crisis. He will give all assistance when needed (Nītiśataka of भर्तृहरि 70).
